label: Q4 launch flags confirmed: claude --help has --session-id, -r/--resume, -c/--continue, --dangerously-skip-permissions, --ax-screen-reader plus --permission-mode bypassPermissions; opencode --help has --standalone, --auto, --session/-s (create or continue); codex --help has --no-alt-screen, --no-daemon, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox and no --session-id, supporting the fixed-session-id claim; pi --help has --session-id, --approve/-a and --tui-mode fullscreen|regular. The four 'High'/'Medium' ratings rest on real flags.

Codex exposes --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, evidence that hooks are gated behind a trust decision. 002's R-002 only anticipates permission and workspace-trust prompts, but its first consumer 043/006 observes nothing except hook output (the decision-capture append and the Stop-hook nudge), so an untrusted-hook prompt reads as an unexpected question and a silently skipped hook yields an all-N/A row with no explanation. Add hook trust to the T001 probe list and to R-002.

The Devin adapter's resume half is unverified: devin --help confirms -r/--resume [<SESSION_ID>] and -c/--continue, but the id comes from 'devin list' (a subcommand whose surface was not checked) and --resume takes an optional id, so 'devin --resume' with no id may open an interactive session picker that is itself a question surface. Two probe items 002 does not list.

Stage marks have no carrier: 002 REQ-010 allows PASS, FAIL, SKIP only, while 006 needs PASS, FAIL, DEVIATION and N/A. SKIP is a runtime-level blocker, not a stage outcome, and neither DEVIATION nor N/A has any producer. 002 emits per-turn pass/fail plus a per-runtime verdict, not a per-stage status file, so 006's four-column checkpoints.tsv is produced by nothing.

006's retry-once on DEVIATION (NFR-R02 and its risk table 'the runner resends the instruction once') is contradicted by 002 REQ-006, 'the first failed turn ends that runtime's run'. 002 has no retry, no attempt counter and no re-send, so implementing it as written makes 006's mitigation impossible.

S0 has no human turn, but 002's turn model is exactly one of send, restart or compact and check runs only after a settled turn, so a stage with no turn has no evidence folder (a turn id names it) and no check. The format needs a check-only stage. 002's baseline is also the repository snapshot while 006's S0 baseline is the scratch project's git status and queue listing.

S8 compacts and then sends in one stage, but 002 gives a turn one action and checks only at the end of a settled turn, so the queue-sha comparison between the compact and the next send has no slot. Splitting S8 into two turns breaks 006's 13-row checkpoints requirement.

S9 restart mismatch: 006 expects /exit then claude --continue, while 002's restart resumes a fixed --session-id via claude --resume <uuid>. Both flags exist but --continue takes the most recent session in the cwd and --resume takes a specific one, so under 002 the session id cannot change, 006's open question answers itself and S9's 'session id recorded' stops being informative.

S12 contradiction: 006 requires a second scratch project with SYSTEM_DECISION_CAPTURE_DISABLED=1 as row 13 of the same scenario, in one checkpoints.tsv, while 002's guidance says a kill-switch run is 'a second scenario whose env sets the switch' and its scratch guard creates exactly one project per runtime. The consumer cannot express its own completion criterion against the producer's documented mechanism.

006 needs 5-15 s of random think time after each turn and 3-8 s after a question widget, from a recorded seed, but 002 offers one fixed delay_ms per turn with no per-question pause, no randomization, no seed, and no required fields in actions.jsonl to record it. The human-pause realism the phase exists to prove is not expressible.

006 counts nudge lines per turn from the pane, but 002 saves a settled-screen capture per turn plus one whole-run raw-pane.log with no per-turn boundaries, so a line printed earlier in the turn can be missed and cannot be cut out of the log. 002 needs per-turn byte offsets into the raw log, or 006 must fall back to counting the nudge file and treat the pane as a presence sample.

REQ-008 cannot detect the failure it exists to catch: git status reports paths and their tracked/untracked/ignored state, never contents, so appending a line to an existing queue file or bumping an existing nudge file produces a byte-identical snapshot. Verified live that 'git status --porcelain --ignored' prints one '!! <path>' per ignored file in .skilled/skills/.state and --ignored=matching prints the same set, so only path creation or deletion is visible. 006's own check is weaker still: it uses git status --short without --ignored, so ignored state files never enter its snapshot. Replace both with a content hash plus line count over the state subtree.

A scratch project outside the repository loses all repo-local runtime config: .claude (agents, commands, hooks, skills, settings.json, mcp.json), .pi (agents, extensions, npm, models.json, mcp.json), .opencode (agents, commands, hooks, plugins, bin), .codex (agents, hooks, hooks.json, prompts, config.toml) and .devin (agents, hooks, skills, config.json, mcp_config.json) all exist at the repository root. 002's setup command is the only channel by which any of it reaches the project, yet 002 neither requires setup for a runtime that needs project-local config nor verifies after it that the config arrived; a runtime starting with no hooks can still report PASS.

Pi is the one runtime that survives losing repo-local config: @juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question is installed repo-locally at .pi/npm/node_modules/@juicesharp and user-globally at ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/@juicesharp, both already recorded in the packet's measured output. Pi can therefore pass a matrix row while a harness setup fault is present in the other four.

direction: Treating SKIP as the carrier for 006's N/A stage marks
reason: SKIP is defined in 002 REQ-010 as a runtime-level blocker (missing binary, runtime not requested, tool the adapter lacks), so mapping it onto a per-stage outcome would make a passing runtime indistinguishable from a skipped stage; the mismatch is a missing status vocabulary, not a naming preference.

direction: Confirming any runtime's question dialog keys from documentation alone
reason: No CLI documents its question dialog text or keys; --help only proves the launch flags exist, which is why 002 ADR-002's recorded-probe approach remains correct and the flags were the only thing checkable read-only this run.
